The passage discusses the emergence of preconquest mentality in a society, specifically in the context of infant care and nurturing practices among the New Guinea forest-dwelling hunter-gatherer-gardeners.
    
    Here is a transcription of the text:
    
    **Spawning Preconquest Consciousness**
    
    Preconquest mentality emerged from a sociosensual infant nurture common to its era but shunned in ours. When I first went into those isolated hamlets in the deep New Guinea forests I was dumbfounded by the lush sensuality of infant care I saw in the southern reaches of what the new Australian administration called 'South Fore'.6
    
    This type of nurture was studied in greatest detail among the New Guinea forest-dwelling hunter-gatherer-gardeners on the southern slopes of the Kratke Range just after Western contact in the early 1960s. They provided the initial model for liminal consciousness. Bordering them to the north were people whose adoption of sweet potato as their staple was despoiling forest lands and undercutting the free range requirement of their traditional preconquest way-of-life. Among them an indigenously emerging supraliminal type of consciousness was coming into being.
    
    In the isolated hamlets in the southern forests, infants were kept in continuous bodily contact with mothers or the mothers' friends--on laps when they were seated, on hips, under arms, against backs, or on shoulders when they were standing. Even during intensive food preparation, or when heavy loads were being moved, babies were not put down. They had priority.
    
    There was always a place for them against the body of a 'mother' or close associate. Loads could be shed or lightened, but babies were simply not put down, not deprived of constant, ever-ready, interactive body contact--even when the group was on the move under difficult conditions. Babies responded to this blanket of ever-ready empathetic tactile stimulation by tactile responses of their own. Very quickly they began assembling a sophisticated tactile-speech to transmit desires, needs, and states of mind. They didn't whine or cry to get attention; they touched. While babies everywhere are liminally aware, the constant empathetic tactile contact required to produce a sophisticated type of preverbal communication is rare--except among preconquest peoples.
    
    Eliciting delight from babies was a desired social norm, and attentive tactile stimulation was the daily lot of infants. It included protracted body-to-body caressing, snuggling, oral sensuality

title: The “Hole” Tweet That Turned Into a Healing Religion
summary:
The most quotable bit was Qiaochu Yuan casually announcing that you can say “hey you know that hole at the center of your being” and people will instantly know what you mean—then immediately escalating it into a claim: you’re *not* born with the hole, it’s what happens when the love/attunement you needed never actually landed. Her follow-up move was to drop the essay “Preconquest Consciousness” as the “what humans look like without the hole” artifact: New Guinea infant care with nonstop body contact, tactile “speech” instead of crying, and a whole social world that’s basically constant nervous-system co-regulation.

The arc: Rich Decibels had already been circling this vibe-y territory (Kastrup’s “Genesis = symbolic thought/the Fall,” plus his own “language inhibits understanding”/“bodies broadcast like radios” threads). Then Qiaochu’s viral “hole” tweet (1.4k likes) gave everyone a sticky handle for the feeling; the essay link made it feel like anthropology-backed evidence. The peak was the therapeutic/practical turn: Qiaochu says MDMA can temporarily show you hole-less life but won’t last unless you do real repair work; she name-drops Ideal Parent Figure Protocol as “most directly hole-filling,” and even warns how “the hole” framing can be weaponized by cult leaders promising they’re the only ones who can fill it. Relic_radiation then made it extremely concrete—claiming 200+ hours of bodywork resolved “half or more” of their developmental trauma, and recommending stuff like Esalen massage, craniosacral, and even cuddle parties as imperfect-but-real substitutes for missing early attunement.

After that, it diffused into a shared memeplex rather than a fight: people kept pulling iconic passages (Qiaochu’s favorite is the hunting party where an arrow silently appears in a boy’s hand and others adjust branches in perfect sync—“individualistic unified at-oneness”). Aleksil connects the “Collapse of Preconquest Consciousness” chapter to Julian Jaynes’ bicameral mind breakdown; Drewface posts a gut-punch “first-hand account of a culture dying in a week” as modernity nukes subtle rapport; Malcolm Ocean tries to operationalize it, first as epistemic humility (“maybe humans can be unfathomably different”), then later as parenting praxis with a newborn—realizing you can’t “go back,” only invite a child into the (modern) culture you actually have, while trying to cultivate more nonverbal play/“we”-mode.

Why care: it’s basically a bridge between existential dread, attachment/developmental trauma, and the feeling that modern life amputated some older human social technology. Even if the anthropology is shaky, the thread’s core utility is giving people a shared language (“the hole”) *and* a menu of interventions (MDMA-as-window, IPFP, bodywork, touch/attunement practices, parenting experiments) while keeping one eye on the dark side—how easily that same longing gets turned into coercion.
